title: Encode postmortem actions into a PRD verification matrix for runtime reliability
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: After the February KV-cache thrashing incident and the cross-region autoscale coldstart outages, we need a concrete way to translate postmortem action items into prescriptive PRD requirements and automated verification steps. This ticket updates the PRD for runtime reliability to include a machine-readable verification matrix (RVM) that maps incident triggers, acceptance criteria, test vectors, and rollout gates to product requirements. The goal is to ensure that postmortem fixes are ship-verified and that future releases cannot regress on the same classes of failure without automated detection and blocker gates.
background_and_context: Two recent incidents (KV-cache thrash and coldstart autoscale mismatch) surfaced gaps between postmortem action items and the acceptance tests used for releases. Current PRDs contain prose-level requirements but lack deterministic verification steps and explicit pass/fail thresholds. Ops playbooks and runbooks survived in docs but were not consistently enforced in release gating. The RVM will be the canonical mapping used by Product, Eng, QA, and SRE for release decisions.
goals: Convert top 8 postmortem action items into actionable PRD requirements
Create a verification matrix (RVM) with test vectors and quantitative pass/fail thresholds
Integrate RVM checks into CI release gating and daily synthetic verification
Reduce recurrence probability for the same incident class by >80% within two releases
non_goals: Re-architecting the serving runtime as part of this ticket
Implementing long-term hardware capacity contracts (business/legal work)
Replacing runbooks with RVM — runbooks remain operational sources of truth
requirements: REQ-001: For each postmortem action, create a one-row mapping in the RVM: incident_trigger, mitigation_requirement, test_vector, pass_threshold, rollback_criteria, owner
REQ-002: RVM must include at least one automated test that can be executed in CI or a synthetic cluster for every high and medium customer_impact action
REQ-003: Define quantitative pass_thresholds: e.g., 95th percentile latency increase <= 15% under synthetic KV-cache stress, error rate < 0.5% for 1 minute during autoscale burst
REQ-004: Add rollout gates that require green RVM results for canary region before global rollout; failed gate must trigger automatic halt and open PR to rollback or mitigation
REQ-005: Track RVM results in Console dashboard; expose per-release boolean and last-run timestamp
REQ-006: Provide an exportable CSV/JSON of RVM for audit and retrospective analysis
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: RVM created in the PRD repo and reviewed by Eng, SRE, and Design; review notes addressed
AC-2: At least 6 postmortem actions (including KV-cache, autoscale coldstart, and multi-model routing fallback) mapped to RVM rows
AC-3: Automated test harness integrated with CI that can run the three high-priority tests in under 30 minutes on the synthetic cluster
AC-4: Canary rollout gate enforces RVM green check prior to promoting canary to global; documented failure path exists
AC-5: Dashboard tile in Console shows last RVM run result and links to artifacts (logs, test harness run IDs)
AC-6: Blameless post-release verification doc created and distributed to stakeholders after first release using the RVM
acceptance_test_vectors: TV-1 (KV-cache thrash): Reproduce 60-second burst of large-token prefix requests with 3x normal concurrency; verify 95p latency < 1.15x baseline and error rate < 0.5%
TV-2 (Autoscale coldstart): Simulate sudden 4x request surge in a cold pool scenario; verify time-to-shed and warm-pool ramp meets SLOs, and request success rate >= 99.2% over 2 minutes

TV-3 (Regional failover): Inject regional latency between services and verify model routing falls back within 2x latency of baseline and no more than 10% of requests degrade quality beyond metric thresholds
tradeoffs_and_considerations: Extra test coverage will increase CI runtime and release time; mitigated by partitioning tests into quick smoke and longer nightly suites
Quantitative thresholds may be conservative initially; allow one release of tuning based on real traffic before locking thresholds
Tighten rollout gates increases safety but may delay fixes reaching customers; plan for emergency bypass process with approvals documented
Maintaining RVM will add product overhead; recommend quarterly RVM review and pruning process
implementation_notes: Owner model: Product owns RVM content; Eng/SRE owns test implementation and CI integration
Storage: RVM stored as YAML/CSV in docs/prd/runtime-rvm/ and linked from PRD; must be machine-parseable
CI: Use synthetic-cluster runner in ENG-44890; add workflow runtime and resource tags for billing visibility
Observability: Add a 1-line telemetry event 'rvm.run' with fields: release_tag,result,run_id,test_ids
rollout_plan: 1) Draft RVM and map initial postmortem items (this ticket)
2) Implement automated tests for top-3 test vectors (ENG lead) and add to CI as gated smoke tests
3) Add a canary release that enforces RVM green for one region for two consecutive canary runs
4) After successful canary, roll out to remaining regions with monitoring and scheduled verification
5) Post-release blameless verification and retrospective to refine thresholds
monitoring_and_alerting: Create RVM dashboard in Console showing per-test pass rate and drift over last 30 days
Alert: test-run-failure for any high-priority TV triggers PagerDuty P1 to on-call SRE
Maintain synthetic verification daily run with auto-retry; persistent failures create a ticket automatically
risks: Risk: False positives on synthetic tests block releases — mitigated via quick bypass with documented approvers and rollback plan
Risk: Test maintenance burden grows — mitigate with ownership and quarterly pruning
Risk: Incomplete mapping misses edge-case incidents — process requires triage meetings to add missing items
